title: Deep learning emergent spacetime from fermionic spectral functions in holography
authors: Koji Hashimoto, Hyun-Sik Jeong, Keun-Young Kim, Daichi Takeda, Kwan Yun
abstract: We present a physics-informed machine learning framework based on Neural Ordinary Differential Equations that solves the holographic inverse problem: reconstructing the bulk spacetime and gauge field of a charged AdS black hole directly from boundary fermionic spectral functions. Encoding the UV asymptotics, horizon regularity, and zero temperature extremality as hard constraints in the neural network architecture, our framework reliably reconstructs the extremal Reissner-Nordström AdS geometry across three quantum critical regimes set by the $U(1)$ probe charge---non-Fermi liquid, marginal Fermi liquid (strange metal), and Fermi-liquid-like states---and can jointly infer the probe charge itself to sub-percent accuracy. Relaxing the near-AdS boundary constraint uncovers a geometrical degeneracy: bulk profiles that differ throughout the radial direction but share the same near-horizon $AdS_2 \times \mathbb{R}^2$ data reproduce identical spectral functions near the Fermi surface. This isospectral non-uniqueness is precisely the bulk degeneracy expected on general holographic grounds at zero temperature, and its spontaneous emergence across independent training runs shows that the network isolates the IR CFT universality rather than overfitting a single UV completion.
summary: This work uses physics-informed machine learning (Neural ODEs) to solve the holographic inverse problem, reconstructing the geometry of a charged AdS black hole from measured fermionic spectral functions. It successfully maps out the physics across three quantum critical regimes, confirming the utility of ML in extracting deep physical structure from boundary data.
main_problem: The paper tackles the holographic inverse problem: reconstructing the bulk spacetime and gauge field of a charged AdS black hole directly from boundary fermionic spectral functions.
main_result: The physics-informed machine learning framework successfully reconstructs the extremal Reissner-Nordström AdS geometry across three distinct quantum critical regimes, demonstrating the network isolates the IR CFT universality.
method: It employs a Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (Neural ODE) framework, constrained by physical boundary conditions, to solve the inverse problem posed by the holographic Dirac equation.
model_or_system: The context is holographic condensed matter theory (AdS/CMT), modeling a probe Dirac fermion in the background of a charged AdS black hole, relevant for studying quantum critical points.
key_observables: Boundary fermionic spectral function, $A(\omega,k) =  rac{1}{\pi} 	ext{Im} G^-(\omega,k)$, and the reconstructed bulk spacetime metrics and gauge fields.
important_parameters: Three quantum critical regimes defined by the $U(1)$ probe charge: non-Fermi liquid, marginal Fermi liquid (strange metal), and Fermi-liquid-like states.
main_assumptions: The framework assumes the validity of the AdS/CFT correspondence and uses hard constraints (UV asymptotics, horizon regularity) within the Neural ODE architecture.
figures_summary: The notes describe figures illustrating the reconstruction of the extremal RN geometry and comparing recovered profiles to known analytical solutions, highlighting the detection of geometrical degeneracy.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure reviewing the holographic Dirac equations, establishing benchmark spectral functions, detailing the Neural ODE framework, demonstrating the reconstruction process, and finally exploring the resulting geometrical degeneracy.
why_interesting: The application of advanced ML techniques to solve fundamental problems in strongly correlated electron physics (strange metals) via holography provides a powerful, modern tool for theoretical condensed matter research.
